subject: MarlinTech inference ops recap + topology commitments
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@marlintech.com>, Samir Desai <samir.desai@marlintech.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Quick recap & next steps — inference ops deep-dive (MarlinTech)

Hi Ellen / Samir,

Thanks again for taking the deep-dive with the team earlier. Below is a concise recap from our side so we have alignment on pain, goals, and the technical commitments we discussed. Please flag anything I missed.

High-level pain points you reiterated
- Critical tail-latency spikes during peak trading windows (0.5–1% of requests blow past SLO and impact UX).
- Cost creep from over-provisioning GPUs for short bursts; inconsistent batching in the current endpoint.
- Model drift: need safe rollback and model-variant routing for A/B tests.

Business goals (targeted for Q2 pilot)
- 99th percentile tail latency <= 350ms for 512-token completions (external-facing API).
- Support sustained 80–120 QPS (small responses) with bursts to 400 QPS for short windows.
- Keep inference cost per 1k tokens under $0.18 during pilot.

Technical notes and proposed topology (what we sketched on the call)
- Primary serving: Dedicated GPU pool in us-west with 4x A100s per shard. Model runtime uses quantized Llama-70B (Q4_0->8-bit plan) for main path; fallback to Llama-13B quantized variant for heavy-concurrency fallbacks.
- Smart routing policy: low-latency route for SLO-critical traffic; cost-aware route for background/async tasks. Automatic fallback to 13B if queue latency > 120ms.
- Caching: prefix KV caching for common prompts (match ratio estimate ~18%); we recommend a short TTL (5–10m) initially.
- Batching: continuous batching with adaptive batch-size knob targeting 120ms batch window during off-peak and 25–40ms during low-latency flows.
- Latency split (budget): model inference ~220ms, network+LB ~40ms, tokenization+post-proc ~40–50ms, safety/filters ~20ms.

Data/security items
- You asked about data residency and logs: pilot will run in your VPC peered to redwood-private (we'll provide the Private deployment package). Audit logs we expose include token counts, route decisions, and model version IDs.
- We confirmed SOC2 + optional encrypted-at-rest keys via customer KMS.

Immediate next actions (owner and ETA)
1) Redwood: produce a staging topology sketch with exact GPU sizing + estimated monthly cost — by Fri 2028-03-24. (Owner: alex_martinez) (Attachment: marlintech-topology-sketch.pdf)
2) MarlinTech: provide a 2-week sample of request traces (anonymized) and the peak window schedule so we can simulate burst scenarios — by Tue 2028-03-28. (Owner: samir.desai@marlintech.com)
3) Joint: run a 48-hour pilot on a canary shard (metrics to watch: 95th, 99th latency, p50 cost/token, KV cache hit rate) — target pilot start week of 2028-04-08. (Owner: joint)

Attachments: marlintech-slo-table.csv (SLO matrix we sketched), marlintech-topology-sketch.pdf (staging topology).

If that all looks right I'll drop a draft mutual action plan into the shared Drive and loop in engineering to book the pilot kickoff.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0132

--
Redwood Inference — production-first inference runtime
From: Samir Desai <samir.desai@marlintech.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Ellen Park <ellen.park@marlintech.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick recap & next steps — inference ops deep-dive (MarlinTech)

Alex — thanks for the clean summary. A few clarifications and one ask: 

1) On the 99th percentile target: the 350ms target looks good as a short-term objective; long-term we'd like to aim for 250–300ms if the canary proves out. Can your cost model show delta between 350ms and 275ms targets (rough per-month estimate)?
2) We'll attach anonymized traces and a CSV of hourly QPS during last month — sharing that by Monday.
3) Regarding KMS integration: can you confirm if Redwood Private supports our AWS KMS cross-account key rotation policy, or do we need to do an alternate flow?

Also, we had an internal ops question: for the fallback to 13B model, will the tokenization and output filtering be identical so we don't introduce downstream schema drift? If not, we need a brief compatibility test.

Attachment: marlintech-request-traces-202803.csv (will be redacted before send).

Samir
Head of Platform Engineering | MarlinTech
samir.desai@marlintech.com
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Samir Desai <samir.desai@marlintech.com>, Ellen Park <ellen.park@marlintech.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 24 Mar 2028 10:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick recap & next steps — inference ops deep-dive (MarlinTech)

Samir — great, appreciate the quick follow. Short answers inline and next coordination steps below.

On cost delta (350ms vs 275ms): we will run a quick sizing exercise and estimate incremental GPU-hours and expected cost impact; I'll include two scenarios (conservative and optimistic) in the Fri deliverable.

KMS cross-account: Redwood Private supports AWS KMS cross-account keys via an IAM role handshake; we'll include the integration checklist (we may need your security team's IAM principal for a one-time setup).

Fallback compatibility: tokenization is identical across the two model variants; however, we do recommend a short compatibility smoke test (10k requests) to validate any subtle decoding differences from quantization. We will add a compatibility test to the pilot plan.

Next coordination items (updated)
- Alex: topology + cost scenarios + integration checklist (Deliverable: 2028-03-24 by EOD) — posted to Drive (link above).
- Samir/MarlinTech: traces + hourly QPS CSV (Deliverable: 2028-03-27).
- Jordan/Redwood infra: prepare a canary shard with Llama-70B quantized image and a 13B fallback image; include KV cache instrumented metrics. (Target: ready by 2028-04-05).

I'll create a short agenda for the pilot kickoff once the topology doc and traces are in place. Thanks again — looping Grace for CS handoff to coordinate the onboarding touches.

Best,
Alex
